{{Short description|American men's college basketball season}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=August 2023}} {{Infobox college sports team season | year = 2023–24 | team = Virginia Cavaliers | sport = basketball | logo = Virginia Cavaliers wordmark.svg | logo_size = 250 | conference = Atlantic Coast Conference | short_conf = ACC | CoachRank = | APRank = | record = 23–11 | conf_record = 13–7 | head_coach = [[Tony Bennett (basketball)|Tony Bennett]] | hc_year = 15th | assoc_coach = Jason Williford | ahc_year = 15th | asst_coach1 = [[Ron Sanchez]] | ac1_year = 10th | asst_coach2 = Orlando Vandross | ac2_year = 6th | arena = [[John Paul Jones Arena]] | champion = | tourney = [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] | tourney_result = First Four | off_scheme = [[Blocker-Mover offense|Blocker-Mover]] | def_scheme = [[Glossary of basketball terms#P|Pack-Line]] | captain = | captain2 = | captain3 = }} {{2023–24 ACC men's basketball standings}} The '''2023–24 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Virginia]] during the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team was led by head coach [[Tony Bennett (basketball)|Tony Bennett]] in his 15th year, and played their home games at [[John Paul Jones Arena]] in [[Charlottesville, Virginia]], as members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. The Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team drew an average home attendance of 13,992 in 17 games in 2023-24, the 17th highest in college basketball.{{Cite web |title=Men's Basketball Attendance Records through 2024-25 |url=http://fs.ncaa.org.s3.amazonaws.com/Docs/stats/m_basketball_RB/Attend.pdf |website=fs.ncaa.org}} The Cavaliers started the season with four straight wins and earned themselves the twenty-fourth spot in the AP Rankings to start the season. They lost the opening game of the [[Fort Myers Tip-Off]] to [[2023–24 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]] and rebounded to defeat [[2023–24 West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball team|West Virginia]] in the third place game. The win wasn't enough to keep them in the rankings, as they fell out ahead of their [[ACC–SEC Challenge]] matchup with fourteenth ranked [[2023–24 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team|Texas A&M]]. They won that match and two more matches to return to the rankings at number twenty-two. They went 1–1 as the 22nd ranked team, losing to twenty-third ranked [[2023–24 Memphis Tigers men's basketball team|Memphis]] before falling out again. The Cavaliers then lost three of their next four ACC games, with the lone win coming against struggling [[2023–24 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Louisville]]. A [[Virginia–Virginia Tech rivalry|rivalry]] win over [[2023–24 Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball team|Virginia Tech]] sparked an eight game winning streak for the Cavaliers as they also defeated [[2023–24 NC State Wolfpack men's basketball team|NC State]] in overtime and [[2023–24 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team|Clemson]] during the stretch. They again returned to the rankings at number twenty-one. They lost to [[2023–24 Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball team|Pittsburgh]] and won a low scoring game against [[2023–24 Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball team|Wake Forest]] before falling out of the rankings again. The Cavaliers finished out the season 2–3 losing a rivalry rematch to Virginia Tech and to [[2023–24 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] and [[2023–24 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]], who were both ranked tenth at the time of the matchup. The Cavaliers finished the season 23–11 and 13–7 in [[2023–24 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in third place. As the third seed in the [[2024 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]], they earned a bye to the Quarterfinals, where they defeated eleventh seed [[2023–24 Boston College Eagles men's basketball team|Boston College]] in overtime before losing to eventual champions NC State in overtime in the Semifinals. They earned a controversial at-large bid to the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] and were placed as a tenth seed in the First Four in the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament#Midwest regional – Detroit, Michigan|Midwest]] region. They lost their matchup with [[2023–24 Colorado State Rams men's basketball team|Colorado State]] 67–42 to end their season. After the game, Virginia was widely criticized for its offensive performance, which included a stretch of nearly 14 minutes of game time and nearly an hour of real time during which they did not score. ==Previous season== The 2022–23 Cavaliers finished the season with a 25–8 record, 15–5 in [[2022–23 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]], to finish in a tie for first place and clinch a share of their sixth regular season title in ten seasons, and their eleventh ACC regular season title in school history. They defeated [[2022–23 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] and [[2022–23 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team|Clemson]] to reach the championship game of the [[2023 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]], where they lost to [[2022–23 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]]. They received a bid to [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 4 seed in the East region, where they were upset in the First Round by [[2022–23 Furman Paladins
